characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616), Doctor Strange (2016); brief 2012 appearance in Avengers: Endgame (2019)
characters.summary: The Ancient One is the Sorcerer Supreme of Kamar-Taj, a master of the mystic arts who uses sling-ring portals, the Mirror Dimension, astral projection, eldritch weapons and shields, and secretly drew on the Dark Dimension to extend her life.

techniques: Forcing others' astral forms out of their bodies

mechanisms: Eldritch shields (blocked an Arrow of Apollon)
Space warping in the Mirror Dimension using Dark Dimension power

weaknesses: Her immortality only suppresses aging; she can still be killed by fatal wounds
Can be caught off guard (Kaecilius stabbed her through the Tall Zealot)
mobility: Sling-ring portals across great distances and between dimensions
Enters the Mirror Dimension without a sling ring
limitations: Must keep drawing on the Dark Dimension to sustain her life
Cannot see the futures past her own death

sources.supports: MCU powers (portals, Mirror Dimension, astral projection, eldritch weapons and shields, Dark Dimension power), weaknesses, the astral push on Strange, and her fights with Kaecilius and the Zealots.

feats.claim: Pushed Doctor Strange's astral form out of his physical body after he touched her.
Blocked an Arrow of Apollon with an eldritch shield while fighting the Dragon Raiders with Mordo.

notableResults.note: In the Mirror Dimension she beat the Tall Zealot and pressured Kaecilius, but he stabbed her through the Tall Zealot; she was kicked back to the Earthly Plane and died in hospital.

conditional.ability: Greatly boosted power and space warping in the Mirror Dimension; suppressed aging

campaignTags.claim: Master of the mystic arts who wields eldritch weapons, shields and Tao fans and manipulates the Mirror Dimension
Opens sling-ring portals to cross great distances and travel between dimensions

unknowns: Levitation/flight is not documented on the MCU wiki page; removed from mobility.
Use of the Eye of Agamotto's time powers is presumed but never shown.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, Earth-828: The Fantastic Four: First Steps (2025), Ben Grimm
characters.summary: Ben Grimm gained super strength and an indestructible rock-like hide from cosmic radiation aboard the Excelsior, and fights alongside the Fantastic Four of Earth-828.

sources.supports: Ben Grimm's origin (cosmic radiation on the Excelsior), super strength and indestructible rock-like hide, and his part in the battle against Galactus.

feats.claim: Helped Reed, Sue and Johnny physically push Galactus toward the teleportation bridge.

notableResults.note: Team effort: the Fantastic Four pushed Galactus toward the teleportation bridge with Sue straining past her limits, and Silver Surfer rammed him through; Grimm's individual contribution is not detailed.

unknowns: The MCU wiki Thing page could not be opened (site error), so specific strength/durability feats and his height are unverified.
Lifting and hurling vehicles (original claim, cited to general comics/media) is not supported by an MCU source; removed.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616), Hope van Dyne: Ant-Man (2015), Ant-Man and the Wasp (2018), Avengers: Endgame (2019)
characters.summary: Hope van Dyne is a lifelong martial artist who uses the Pym Particle Wasp Suit to shrink while keeping her full-size strength, fly on four artificial wings, and fire energy bolts and Pym disks from her gauntlet stingers.

techniques: Energy bolts / concussive streams from gauntlet stingers
Shrinking strikes that gain force as she regrows
Mixed martial arts (muay Thai, Brazilian jiu-jitsu, judo, kickboxing, aikido)

mechanisms: Shrinking makes her a tiny, hard-to-hit target while retaining full-size durability

weaknesses: Phasing opponents can pass through her stinger shots (Ghost)
mobility: Wing flight at up to 125 mph in the suit
limitations: Flight, shrinking and stingers depend on the Wasp Suit

sources.supports: Hope van Dyne's Wasp Suit (shrinking, wings, gauntlet blasts, Pym disks), martial arts, infiltration feats and fights with Burch's men, Ghost and alternate Thanos's army.

feats.claim: Shrank and flew through Cassie's school with Lang to recover the old suit.
Knocked out Sonny Burch's goons at his restaurant using size changes, including an enlarged salt shaker.
Her stinger blasts, combined with Shuri's and Pepper Potts's, knocked alternate Thanos down at the Battle of Earth.

notableResults.note: Defeated them at the restaurant with size changes and kitchen items and kept the component.
After Starr knocked out Hope and Pym at the hideout, Hope defeated her with her stingers and took the lab back. Other encounters with Ghost were not wins.

campaignTags.claim: Flies on four artificial insect wings built into the Wasp Suit (up to 125 mph)
Shrinks using Pym Particles while keeping full-size strength and durability
Relies on the Pym-tech Wasp Suit, stingers and Pym disks
Shrank to slip through Cassie's school and hid in a chandelier at Burch's restaurant

unknowns: Stinger blasts are described as energy bolts / concussive streams, not bio-electric; the 'bio-electric' wording was removed.
Ant-Man and the Wasp: Quantumania (2023) is not covered by the opened page.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe, What If...? (animated, 2021-2024), Uatu
characters.summary: Uatu is a Watcher who observes the multiverse from the Observational Plane, with superhuman physical attributes, force fields, telekinesis and a golden armor form, but is sworn to observe and not intervene.
weaknesses: His oath often stops him from acting
Was outmatched one-on-one by Infinity Ultron
mobility: Travels between universes via the Nexus and the Observational Plane
limitations: Oath of non-interference: he must only observe

sources.supports: Uatu's powers, oath, multiverse travel, transport of others, the fight with Infinity Ultron and recruiting the Guardians of the Multiverse.

feats.claim: Observes and affects universes across the multiverse through the Observational Plane's Nexus.
Recruited the Guardians of the Multiverse with Strange Supreme's help to stop Infinity Ultron.

notableResults.citation: What If...? Season 1 ('What If... Ultron Won?')
notableResults.note: Ultron beat him across multiple universes and tried to crush his head; Uatu broke free by punching Ultron's arm and escaped to Strange Supreme, then gathered the Guardians.

campaignTags.claim: Telekinesis is listed among his powers
Transported Captain Carter, Black Widow and others between universes

unknowns: Episode numbers are not stated on the opened page; the Ultron fight is cited to the 'What If... Ultron Won?' arc.
'Cosmic energy projection' was not supported and was removed.
The season 3 confrontation with Eminence, Incarnate and Executioner (who blasted him into the Observational Plane wall) and the later battle are not detailed on the page.

characters.summary: Thena is an Eternal warrior who manifests any handheld weapon from cosmic energy, with Eternal physiology and master combat skill, but suffers from Mahd Wy'ry.

techniques: Cosmic-energy weapons (spears, swords, shields, knives, axes, staffs) that change form instantly

mechanisms: Eternal physiology with a healing factor

weaknesses: Mahd Wy'ry episodes make her turn on allies
Outmatched by Ikaris in brute force
limitations: Mahd Wy'ry causes memory loss and loss of control

sources.supports: Thena's powers, Mahd Wy'ry, mobility and her fights with Deviants, Kro, Gilgamesh and Ikaris.

feats.claim: Killed dozens of Deviants over the centuries with cosmic-energy weapons.
Withstood the force of Kro after he absorbed Gilgamesh's powers and blocked his sneak attack.

notableResults.note: Killed Kro during the battle against Ikaris, avenging Gilgamesh.
During a Mahd Wy'ry episode he subdued her unharmed; he was holding back.
Fought him evenly for a while before being subdued one-on-one; later, with Makkari and Phastos, she landed blows on him.

characters.continuity: Marvel Cinematic Universe (Earth-616), Thor (2011) through Thor: Love and Thunder (2022)
characters.summary: Thor is the Asgardian God of Thunder, with superhuman strength and durability, lightning generated from his own body, unaided flight, and the weapons Mjølnir and Stormbreaker.

techniques: Mjølnir and Stormbreaker strikes and throws

mechanisms: Survived the full power of a star while forging Stormbreaker

weaknesses: Overconfidence: struck Thanos in the chest to taunt him instead of finishing him
Can be disabled by an Obedience Disk (Sakaar)
mobility: Unaided flight after unlocking his full powers
limitations: Mjølnir requires worthiness; he was briefly unworthy to lift it

sources.supports: MCU Thor's powers (lightning from his body, flight), Stormbreaker forging, and his fights with Hulk, Hela, Thanos, Gorr, the Destroyer and Loki.

feats.claim: Held Nidavellir's iris open and took the full brunt of the star's power to light the forge for Stormbreaker, leaving him severely charred and unconscious.
Summoned lightning without Mjølnir to blast Hela from the Rainbow Bridge.

notableResults.note: Deflected its energy beam back into its head, disabling it.
Contest of Champions on Sakaar: Thor was winning until the Grandmaster activated his Obedience Disk, and Hulk landed the final blow.
Lost an eye to her; he had Loki unleash Ragnarök, which destroyed Asgard and killed Hela. Not a direct one-on-one win.
Utterly defeated by Thanos aboard the Statesman.
In Wakanda he struck Thanos in the chest with Stormbreaker, but Thanos still snapped his fingers.
Battle of Earth: Thanos knocked Thor out; Iron Man later used the Stones to end Thanos and his army.
With Jane Foster, at the cost of her life; ended at the Gates of Eternity.

conditional.ability: Flight before unlocking his full powers

campaignTags.claim: After unlocking his full powers he can hover, glide and fly at great speeds without outside help
Generates incredible amounts of electrical energy from his own body

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics (Earth-616), Thor (2020) #1-6 by Donny Cates; comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: Herald of Thunder is the form Thor took when Galactus imbued him with the Power Cosmic and made him his herald against the Black Winter, rejuvenating him and restoring his lost eye and arm.

techniques: Power Cosmic added to his existing Asgardian abilities

mechanisms: Asgardian durability augmented by the Power Cosmic

limitations: Bound to serve Galactus as herald, an arrangement Thor resisted
characters.formDifferences: Galactus added the Power Cosmic to Thor's existing abilities. The transformation reversed his age, restored his lost eye and arm, and appeared to change Mjolnir. Base MCU Thor has none of this.

sources.supports: Names the form 'Herald of Thunder'; Galactus transforms Thor with the Power Cosmic and restores his severed arm in Thor #1 (2020).
Thor gains the Power Cosmic as Galactus's herald and is rejuvenated with his eye and arm restored; Mjolnir appears changed.
Power Cosmic added to Thor's abilities; Thor executes Galactus and uses his body as a cosmic bomb against the Black Winter.
Herald period: led Galactus to five planets, drove back the Black Winter, stripped and drained Galactus, used him as a bomb.

feats.claim: Used Galactus's body as a cosmic bomb, reducing the Black Winter to a mere snowflake.
Stripped Galactus of the power he had taken from five planets and drained him.

notableResults.note: Thor passed judgment on Galactus and executed him.
Drove back the Black Winter's shades of his greatest enemies, then destroyed it with Galactus as a bomb.

unknowns: Comics form, not MCU: no MCU appearance.

The opened sources do not describe this form's flight, lightning output or how and when Thor lost the Power Cosmic; the original 'cosmic lightning' and 'cosmic flight' claims and the electric-control and natural-flight tags were removed.
A clash with Beta Ray Bill that destroyed Stormbreaker is mentioned on the Earth-616 page, but whether it happened in this form is unclear.

characters.continuity: Marvel Comics, Earth-14412 (Thor: God of Thunder #1, 2012, and later King Thor stories); comics form, not MCU
characters.summary: King Thor is a far-future All-Father version of Thor, one-eyed and with a Destroyer prosthetic arm, who commands the Thor-Force (formerly the Odin-Power) inherited from his father.
limitations: Needed the Forever Sleep to recover after his battle with Doom
characters.formDifferences: An aged future Thor who rules as All-Father with the Thor-Force (the renamed Odin-Power), one eye and a Destroyer arm, and later the Phoenix Force through Mjolnir. Base MCU Thor has none of this.

sources.supports: King Thor's Thor-Force, flight via Mjolnir, Destroyer arm, All-Black use and his fights with Gorr, Galactus, Doom and Old Man Phoenix.
Thor-Power (previously the Odin-Power), fights with the Black Berserkers, Gorr and Galactus, and the Necrosword.
King Thor's origin on Earth-14412, the Thor Force, his restoration of Earth and his Phoenix-powered battle with Doom.

feats.claim: Threw Gorr's entire planet into a black hole with the Necrosword.
His blood restored plant life to Earth after his battle with Galactus.
Fought Doom for 99 years and finally smashed him into New Midgard's mantle with Phoenix Force power.

notableResults.note: Team effort with his two past selves; earlier Gorr defeated him and nailed him to a comet.
Galactus knocked him into deep space; he returned with All-Black and repelled Galactus from Earth.
After Doom's Penance Stare incapacitated him, Logan moved the Phoenix Force into Mjolnir and Thor ended their 99-year battle.
Old Man Phoenix won and stopped short of killing him.
Overtaken by them after a long battle, though not killed.

conditional.dependsOn: Phoenix Force transferred into Mjolnir by Logan

unknowns: Comics form, not MCU: no MCU appearance.
The opened sources do not describe King Thor's lightning or weather control, or call the Thor-Force spellcasting; the electric-control and magic tags and 'reality-altering spells' were removed.
'Odinforce slumber requirements' replaced by the documented Forever Sleep after the Doom battle.
